summary: Stepping Stones Light off Kings Point in Long Island Sound: an 1877 brick keeper's house and tower on the reef, a 1934 ice siege, automated 1966, owned by the Town of North Hempstead since 2008.

light.characteristic: Flashing green every 4 seconds (current, per the town fact sheet; the record's Oc G 4s is not verified)

lens.note: Fifth order, fixed red, 1877 (town; USLHS); fourth order, fixed green, 1932 (town); modern optic from the 1966 automation (town)

structures.note: Square brick tower attached to the keeper's dwelling; 36 ft from base of structure to centre of lantern (USLHS)
Square red-brick dwelling with a mansard roof on a granite platform over riprap (town fact sheet); dwelling completed January 1877

access.note: USLHS record: Open to Public: No. The Town of North Hempstead has owned the lighthouse since 2008; the U.S. Coast Guard maintains the beacon.

visit.note: Not open to visitors (USLHS record). The town's photo captions say it can be seen from the Throgs Neck Bridge.

facts.agency: Town of North Hempstead (owner since 2008); U.S. Coast Guard maintains the beacon

events.note: $6,000 first allocated in June 1866 for a day beacon on the reef and a light near Hart Island; the light later moved to Stepping Stones
Construction begun by A. D. Cook in late 1875; 900 tons of boulders barged to the site 1875-1878
Dwelling completed January 1877 (1876 carved on the tower panel)
First shown the night of 1 March 1877
About 300 tons of riprap placed for the protection of the pier (Light-House Board, item 271)
Efficiency pennant awarded to keeper Ernest Bloom for fiscal 1912
28 July 1921: keeper Stephen Holm rescues two men whose canoe capsized near the light; they are landed at City Island
18 July 1923: keeper Stephen Holm rescues two men from the sailboat Mistral on the rocks east of the light
February-March 1934 cold and ice; keeper unable to land; distress signals 1 March; food sent by the tender Hickory (Bulletin) / depot sent Hickory (town)
Automated October 1966; flashing fixed green optic placed in the lantern room
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, 15 September 2005 (NRHP 05001026)
Coast Guard deems the station surplus and offers it at no cost to eligible entities
Transferred to the Town of North Hempstead; the Coast Guard still maintains the functioning beacon
Stepping Stones Lighthouse Preservation Society established with the town's help; excursion to inspect inside and out on 1 July 2012

corrections.why: USLHS gives 36 ft from base of structure to centre of lantern (about 11 m). The record's 14.0 m matches the 45.5 ft height of the light above mean high water, which is the focal height.
The town fact sheet (which gives Light List number 21505) states 'Flashing green every 4 seconds'. The Light List itself was not read; verify before changing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive spells the first keeper's name Finlay Fraser; the town fact sheet spells it Findlay Fraser. The story follows the archive and notes the variant.

The fact sheet says the dwelling was completed in January 1877 although 1876 is carved on the tower; the light was first shown on 1 March 1877. The record's 1877 build and first-lit dates agree with that.

notes_for_editor: (1) The 1934 ice event is told two ways. The Bulletin (PDF p. 6, printed p. 172, page image checked) says a small tanker bound for New York hailed the keeper, that he had food for another day or two, and that the tender Hickory was sent the same day; it does not name the keeper. The town fact sheet names keeper Charles A. Rogers (the roster agrees, 1924-1934) and a tug, the Muxpet, that broke through the ice, and says Rogers refused food and asked the St. George depot to be told. The story gives both and does not settle the vessel or the food. (2) The fact sheet's notes on Bloom, Holm and the 1934 winter are headed 'From the United States Coast Guard Website'; the sheet gives no page address, so the story says so. The Bulletin 1921 (PDF p. 36, printed p. 196) and Bulletin 1923 (PDF p. 32) entries were checked: 1921 says 'in the vicinity of the light station' (so 'near the light' is supported); 1923 says the sailboat Mistral was 'sinking rapidly' and that the keeper towed the boat to a beach in Long Island. The 1912 Bulletin (PDF p. 47, printed p. 47, page image checked) lists 'Stepping Stones ... Ernest Bloom' in the District 3 row of the efficiency-pennant table. (3) First keeper spelled Finlay Fraser (archive) and Findlay Fraser (town). (4) Record height 14.0 m and characteristic Oc G 4s are contested by the USLHS and the town; see corrections. The Light List was not read. (5) Charles Redfern (roster 1903-1910) also appears in a 1920 Commissioner list as keeper of Point Comfort Light, N.J.; no link is made. Edward M. Grant appears in the Commissioner's 1916 and 1917 'saving of life' lists; the nature of his assistance is not legible, so it is not used. (6) The NRHP nomination (05001026) is not digitised at npgallery (placeholder); the NRHP date is from the town fact sheet. (7) The USCG Historian's Stepping Stones page was not read (no archived copy located). (8) LighthouseFriends and Wikipedia were not quoted. (9) Newspapers: a 1934 search for 'Stepping Stones' with 'Rogers' in New York papers returned no hits; a 1877 search returned pages that contain the phrase but none about the light, so none was used. (10) Roster lines for keepers who served after about 1960 are reproduced as the archive prints them and are not narrated in the story. (11) other_stations not researched. (12) The 1895 item 271 is on scan page 248 (the story now cites it).
